title: Assessing the limitations of the Banister model in monitoring training
authors: Hellard P, Avalos M, Lacoste L, Barale F, Chatard JC, Millet GP
population: Nine elite swimmers, one season of training load and performance data
findings: Performances were related to training loads for all participants (R2 = 0.79 +/- 0.13, P < 0.05) and the estimation procedure seemed stable (leave-one-performance-out).
The 95% bootstrap CIs of the parameters most useful for monitoring were wide: t(a) = 38 (17, 59), t(f) = 19 (6, 32), t(n) = 19 (7, 35), t(g) = 43 (25, 61) days.
Some parameters were highly correlated (ill-conditioning), which the authors say makes their interpretation worthless.
Modelled performance related to training load for all participants (R2 = 0.79 +/- 0.13, P < 0.05) and the estimation procedure seemed stable.
95% bootstrap confidence intervals of the key parameters were wide: ta = 38 (17, 59), tf = 19 (6, 32), tn = 19 (7, 35), tg = 43 (25, 61).
Some parameters were highly correlated (ill-conditioning), making their interpretation worthless; the authors review alternative methods for modelling the training-performance relationship.
limitations: Elite swimmers only, nine athletes, one season; no running or ultra-endurance data. Re-classified from retrospective-cohort to modelling: the study is a statistical analysis of the model's accuracy, ill-conditioning and stability.
implications: Report parameter estimates with bootstrap intervals; do not display or act on fitness/fatigue time constants as precise personal values (95% CI widths here were about 26-42 days).

Constrain or regularise parameters (informative priors, fixed time constants within physiological ranges) when fewer than a season of dense performance tests exist, and do not interpret correlated parameters individually.

If a CTL/ATL/TSB display is offered, use fixed population time constants (conventionally ~42 and ~7 days; convention, not from this paper) and label it a descriptive trend, not fitted individual parameters.
Never present TSB/form as a precise readiness or taper-timing prediction; use fixed taper rules instead.
If individual fitting is ever added, report bootstrap intervals and fall back to defaults when intervals are wide.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, J Sports Sci, 2006, six authors. All numbers match the Europe PMC abstract. CI widths recomputed: ta 42, tf 26, tn 28, tg 36 days (researcher's '20-40' corrected to 26-42).
